thread:
maya: Heads-up 1: I opened a docs PR with embedding-shard guidance + a short migration checklist for shardable models (nebula3b, nova-embeds, etc.). Need eyes on limits, compatibility notes, and the SDK snippets. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/789 :memo:

alvin: On it. Can you paste the key bench numbers and the assumptions (batch size, hw)? Also wondering if SDK should default to `shard_count=1` or `auto`?

maya: Bench summary (artifact): avg latency per embed (batch=8192 tokens): ~12ms/shard on A100, throughput ~85k embeds/s across 8 shards, memory per shard ~6.2GB. I left SDK default explicit at `shard_count=1` in examples so behavior is not surprising. Assumptions noted in PR description.

samir: Compatibility note: Dedicated customers who pin variants could see KV coldstart penalties if they flip `shard_count` up without prewarming. Recommend a short "Pre-warm / Cache" blurb in Compatibility. :warning:

sophia: Rewrote SDK snippets to include `shard_count` for python + ts and added a fallback example. Please sanity-check formatting + comment text. Snippets below:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['RW_KEY'])
resp = client.embeddings.create(model='nebula3b', input=['hello','world'], shard_count=4)
# consumer: aggregate per-doc vectors from 4 shards (e.g., concat/mean)
```

```ts
import { Redwood } from '@redwoodai/sdk'
const rw = new Redwood(process.env.RW_KEY)
const resp = await rw.embeddings.create({ model: 'nebula3b', input: ['hello','world'], shard_count: 4 })
// flatten/aggregate per-doc vectors as needed
```

doc-bot: lint-check: passed. link-checker: 1 broken link found -> `/model-catalog/nebula3b` should be `/models/nebula3b`. Auto-fixed in PR diff.

kai: Numbers look sane. Add a worked cost example (USD / 1M queries) so users can compare shard vs single-shard cost. I can draft it if you want.

maya: I added a short worked example and a tiny table: 1M queries, avg tokens=64 -> estimated cost using current pricing assumptions: 4 shards = $X, 1 shard = $Y. Also added a migration checklist (in PR):
- export existing vectors (CLI snippet)
- choose `shard_count` by throughput vs cost goals
- backfill re-encoded vectors (run as background job with backpressure)
- update retrieval to aggregate shard outputs
- run eval prompt set to guard recall regressions

Is that too prescriptive?

samir: Not too prescriptive. Add a note: "To maintain backwards compatibility, optionally serve both single-shard and sharded indexes during transition." Also call out runtime fallback behavior when query-time `shard_count` mismatches: runtime will fall back to scalar retrieval (documented) instead of failing. :thumbsup:

sophia: For naming consistency, we standardized on `shard_count` across docs and SDKs (not `shards`). Adjusted TS snippet to show an async iterator pattern and included a tiny helper to merge per-shard vectors.

maya: Fixed wording per comments, corrected the broken link, and added the Dedicated coldstart pointer (internal pre-warm script). Will merge after two approvals. @alvin @kai PTAL when you can. Targeting 2026-04-01 model-catalog refresh.

alvin: LGTM from docs side. One grammar nit in the checklist; will approve once CI is green.

doc-bot: merge queued. Auto-merge will attempt in 2 hours if approvals >=2 and CI green.

maya: Thanks all 1: Great quick turn. I left the PR description with a short note about monitoring (recall, latency, cost) during the backfill period and a pointer to the eval harness for regression tests.
